_comment: Model manifest -- the fleet's shared index of large model files.
WHY THIS EXISTS, and what it deliberately is NOT.
It is NOT shared storage for inference. Workers never read model files:
ggml-rpc-server contains no GGUF loading code at all. The coordinator
reads the GGUF and pushes tensors over TCP; workers only keep a local
content-hashed tensor cache (rpc-server -c), measured at ~76% of their
share of the model. So only ONE machine ever needs the full file.
It exists because re-fetching a large model is the slowest thing in this
project. Measured 21 MB/s from HuggingFace -- 7.2 hours for 547 GB. The
same file over gigabit LAN is ~1.4 hours. So: record which node holds
which model, and pull from a peer instead of the internet.
The manifest lives in git rather than on a fileserver. That is the
'shared storage without a NAS' part -- the INDEX is replicated to every
node by the repo, while the BYTES stay on whichever node has the disk.
'entrypoint' is the file to pass to -m. llama.cpp finds sibling parts of
a split GGUF automatically, so it is always part 00001.
'active_params' and 'bytes_per_weight' let cluster/models.sh predict
tok/s from measured bandwidth -- generation runs at ~99% of STREAM, so
tok/s ~= bandwidth / (active_params * bytes_per_weight). See
docs/measurements.md.

models.notes: Smoke-test model. Reasoning model -- budget max_tokens for thinking or it returns empty content (FINDINGS F21).
Model A -- single-node speed reference. Native MXFP4; the F16 GGUF keeps MXFP4 MoE weights.
Interim large model while the coordinator disk is too small for Model B. Only 3B active, so the fastest large model this hardware can run.
Model B -- the thesis. NOT YET FETCHED: needs 547 GB and the coordinator has 431 GB free (FINDINGS F16). Run the coordinator on whichever node gets the big disk.
